frontmatter.title: BRI: a franchise priced for a broken credit cycle
frontmatter.summary: We keep BBRI at BUY with a twelve-month value of Rp4,176, a 61.5% total return from Rp2,820. The shares cost 1.3x forward book for a bank that earned 17.7% in FY2025 and 18.1% in the nine months to September. This revision re-anchors the capital path on management's stated risk appetite and drops a probability claim the three-state table cannot carry.
thesis: Micro is the franchise and the problem: BRI lends where the system will not, at yields the corporate book cannot match, so losses rather than margins set the return.
Credit cost is the swing factor. We hold it near the top of its observed range through the cycle, and that choice accounts for most of the gap between our value and the price.

The dividend is the return anchor. At the 92.0% payout actually distributed the shares yield 13.5% at today's price; the capital cost of that payout is paid by a slower loan-growth glide, now stopped at management's stated risk appetite rather than near the regulatory floor.
The multiple embeds a perpetual return below the 17.7% reported in FY2025 and the 18.1% of the nine months; that gap is the investment case.
The peer screen is the main risk: BRI trades above the median large bank despite a lower return and higher credit cost, so part of the upside needs the sector de-rating to unwind.

blocks.text: Update, 12 November 2026. The policy news is a ceiling raise, not a KUR raise: the 2027 programme-credit ceiling was set at IDR386.90tn, of which KUR takes IDR325.00tn, level with the IDR325.00tn target just set for 2026 and up from IDR295.00tn [S21][S22]. Programme credit had drawn IDR300.80tn of its IDR337.40tn 2026 ceiling by 31 October, leaving IDR36.60tn for the last two months [S21]. The envelope grows while the KUR line does not, so our growth comes from Kupedes, SME and consumer rather than a rising quota, and the extra envelope is itself subsidised credit at programme loss rates [S21][S22]. OJK's NTT scheme sets borrower margins at zero next year and 3.0% in 2028 [S18], and Danantara has asked BRI to lend to farmers at about 9.0% through 13,000 cooperatives [S19]; neither discloses a lender subsidy, so both stay in the risks.

Two things changed in this revision, both about capital. We now anchor the capital path on management's stated 19.0% risk appetite rather than ending near the regulatory floor [S3]: the bank-only ratio runs below the consolidated one, 23.0% against 25.4% at end-2025 and 20.6% against 23.0% at September [S15 p10], so the individual-perimeter equivalent is the mid-teens, and loan growth now tapers from FY2030E to stop there. The estimated ratio troughs at 16.7% and recovers to 17.0%, against a floor of the 9.6% risk-profile CAR plus the 2.5% conservation buffer and the 2.5% systemic surcharge [S15 p10]. Terminal growth stays 1.8%, the rate retention funds. Second, we no longer attach a probability to a flat-multiple outcome: the weighted target covers bear, base and bull only, as set out below.

We keep BUY with a twelve-month value of Rp4,176, a 61.5% total return from Rp2,820, of which Rp379 is the dividend. At 1.3x forward book the market pays for a perpetual return below the 17.7% of FY2025 [S15]. Credit cost at 3.2% then 3.4%, a margin that gives up little after the KUR rotation, and the 92.0% payout carry the value. Even the bear is worth Rp2,908 in twelve months, above the Rp2,820 price before its dividend; the bull is Rp4,872. The Rp379 dividend is 13.5% at today's price, which is why we hold the payout and include the IDR1.00tn buyback [S16].

We would step back if micro formation re-accelerates while the book shrinks, if double-digit growth at this payout takes the individual ratio through the floor or forces a raise, or if deposits trail the system for two consecutive quarters.

Bank Rakyat Indonesia is the largest lender by loan book and the only large bank built on village microcredit. At end-FY2025 it carried gross loans of IDR1,460.73tn and deposits of IDR1,466.84tn, an LDR of 99.6%, on equity of IDR324.03tn [S6][S4]. The government holds 53.2% through Danantara and the public 46.8% [S3]. Micro is the largest segment and the source of both the margin premium and the losses: KUR reached IDR293.40tn, up 10.2%, while Kupedes fell 20.4% to IDR153.50tn; KUR carries a government guarantee and a capped rate, so its margin and risk are lower [S4].

The income statement needs the same perimeter care. The pack's net interest income of IDR136.85tn plus non-interest income of IDR50.03tn is the conventional view; the filing's other operating income is IDR53.68tn. The model's perimeter bridge of IDR21.09tn is not other non-operating income: sharia income less expense, insurance and gold account for three of its four components, and the fourth is the residual between the filing's other operating income and the pack's NOII. It is projected with revenue, from IDR22.77tn to IDR35.06tn [S6].

BRI began as a savings institution for civil servants in the colonial administration and was repurposed before becoming the state vehicle for subsidised microcredit. Its village units and agent network gave it a distribution cost base that urban banks could not replicate.

System loans grew 13.3% in the year to September while deposits grew 8.2% [S8]. Corporate credit grew far faster than MSME and state-owned banks faster than the system, so BRI's core is the slowest-growing part of the market and its challenger segments the fastest [S8]. BRI's share was 15.4% at end-2025 [S3], while third-quarter third-party funds grew 12.0% to IDR1,651.00tn ahead of the system, with CASA at 70.0% [S14][S8].

BRI leads the segment with the highest yields and loss rates and is a challenger where spreads are thin. Its moat is distribution and the deposit franchise built on it, a cost moat because the KUR rate is administered and the micro borrower is price-sensitive [S4]. Fintech lenders compete without the branch cost but also without the deposit base.

Regulation cuts both ways: the administered KUR rate protects volume but caps revenue per loan, and capital rules constrain risk-weighted growth [S4]. The conventional reserve requirement was cut to 7.0% from 1 November 2026 [S17]. KUR disbursed IDR265.90tn by late October and the 2027 programme ceiling is IDR386.90tn, but the KUR allocation of IDR325.00tn is flat on the raised IDR325.00tn 2026 target [S20][S21][S22]. The bull rests on the guarantee and the programme's 2.1% reported loss rate; the bear on the cap and the direction of policy.

Return on equity was 19.7% in FY2023, 19.1% in FY2024 and 17.7% in FY2025 [S6]. Provisions rose from IDR35.81tn in FY2021 to IDR46.72tn in FY2025, the FY2021 stress year carrying them at roughly the same share of the book [S3][S6]. Operating income rose from IDR173.00tn to IDR186.88tn and expenses from IDR82.10tn to IDR88.45tn, leaving pre-provision profit of IDR98.43tn; provisions of IDR46.72tn and the perimeter bridge of IDR21.09tn took pre-tax profit to IDR72.79tn and attributable profit to IDR56.65tn, EPS Rp374 [S6]. The bridge is the least evidenced line in the forecast but it closes the chain to the filing.

The margin needs care because four figures circulate: the pack's 7.1%, our 7.0%, the company's half-year 7.7% and the LK's nine-month 6.2% against 6.5% a year earlier [S6][S4][S15]. The LK's printed margin cannot be net interest income over average earning assets on its own P&L: its interest income less interest expense, annualised, implies a margin well above the printed KPI. We treat the LK line as a bank-basis measure the consolidated statements do not reconcile and anchor on the pack's series, carrying the year-on-year compression the LK does show and taking 7.0% to 6.7% by FY2030E [S15]. With CASA near 70.0% and the reserve cut to 7.0% [S17], the residual easing is the tail of the Kupedes-to-KUR rotation.

Loans grow 10.0% in FY2026E to IDR1,606.80tn, the top of guidance [S4][S15], then at the 8.0% plan rate to IDR2,052.31tn, before tapering to the 1.6% that retention funds and reaching IDR2,409.41tn [S4]. The taper is the capital constraint, not a demand call: at the plan rate the individual ratio would run through the floor, so growth gives way and the 92.0% payout is left intact, stopping the ratio at a 16.7% trough that recovers to 17.0% [S3][S15 p10]. Deposits grow from IDR1,657.53tn to IDR2,318.03tn, so the LDR holds near 96.9%; margin eases from 7.0% to 6.7%; cost-to-income improves from 47.5% to 46.5%; and credit cost is 3.2% then 3.4% through the cycle [S4].

Credit cost is set above the nine-month print for coverage, not from a forecast of deterioration. FY2025 ran at 3.4% of average loans [S6], while the half year improved to 3.1% and micro cost of credit to 3.8%; but micro is still 43.4% of loans at a higher loss rate, and the fourth quarter has carried the year's heaviest charge in each of the last two. The FY2026E rate implies a Q4 charge in line with that seasonality and loan growth.

Coverage is the test. NPL coverage fell from 229.1% in FY2023 to 180.2% at 1H26 while write-offs ran at IDR35.70tn in FY2023 and IDR21.50tn in 1H26 [S4]. The stock ratio rose while formation improved because write-offs, though higher than the prior quarter at IDR5.31tn, still ran below the flow - optics-class, disclosed and above the minimum, not manipulation-class. Our through-cycle cost of risk assumes coverage stabilises near the 1H26 level; rebuilding to FY2023 would cost more. Loans at risk of 9.5% against gross NPL of 3.1% [S15] is the restructured book coverage does not capture.

Micro formation fell from 6.6% to 4.1%, special-mention loans from 6.6% to 5.1% and micro cost of credit from 4.6% to 3.8% [S4]: a turn one year old, not complete. Parent profit of IDR47.69tn for the nine months [S15] tracks the IDR62.48tn we carry, with loans of IDR1,583.77tn below the full-year forecast and deposits of IDR1,651.00tn already near December [S15][S14]. The fourth-quarter provision is the test.

Return on equity rises from 19.0% to 22.3% and 23.0% on a payout held at 92.0%, and part of that uplift is leverage: as the individual ratio falls from 20.0% to its trough, the same return on assets is earned on a thinner equity base. Capital is tested where the regulator tests it. The company reports consolidated KPMM of 23.0% and individual KPMM of 20.6% at 30 September 2026, and the minimum applies to the individual ratio: the 9.6% risk-profile CAR plus the 2.5% conservation buffer plus the 2.5% systemic surcharge [S15 p10]. Risk density is calibrated on the bank-only perimeter so the estimate reproduces that ratio by construction [S15]. On that basis the ratio falls from 20.0% to a 16.7% trough and recovers to 17.0%, above the mid-teens equivalent of the 19.0% appetite the company states [S3], as growth glides to the 1.6% that retained earnings fund [S4]. The FY2025A estimate sits under the filing's 23.0% because bank-only RWA grew faster than consolidated loans over the nine months; the valuation date is exact.

Opening equity is restated from the filing, not bridged with a plug. Parent equity at 30 September 2026 is IDR338.86tn, of which the revaluation surplus is IDR19.86tn [S15]; opening FY2025 parent equity is IDR324.03tn [S6]. The nine-month movement is parent profit IDR47.69tn less dividends paid IDR52.10tn, which carry the FY2025 final tranche and the IDR20.61tn interim paid on 15 January 2026, and other comprehensive income of IDR-2.36tn [S15]; the balances close to within treasury-share and reserve movements the LK does not itemise. ROE is 19.0% on average parent equity, while the filing's 18.1% uses total equity including minorities. The pack records only the final FY2025 tranche; the full year was Rp346, of which Rp137 was the interim [S4][S7].

Residual income is the engine, as the house card requires: half the weight, warranted price-to-book three tenths and the dividend discount model a fifth. All three use the same cost of equity, so the differences are about the return path, not the discount rate. The default weighting put P/B at half and made the lowest method the anchor; this weighting corrects that.

The cost of equity is built from observable inputs. The risk-free rate is the ten-year government bond yield of 7.45% [S9]; the default spread of 1.62% and the country risk premium of 2.46% come from the country-risk table [S10]. The formula then gives 12.45%. With that beta the sum falls below the house floor for Indonesian banks, so the premium lifts it to the floor.

The sustainable return is built from the margin, the balance sheet and the cost lines: in FY2026E a margin of 7.0% on earning assets close to seven times equity, plus non-interest income, less operating expenses and provisions, produces the 19.0% of FY2026E. The multiple is fed the 19.6% average of the model's own FY2026E-FY2028E returns, not the FY2023-FY2025 history of 19.7%, 19.1% and 17.7%: the forward years are the first in which the micro mix has stabilised after the FY2025 credit-cost peak [S6][S4]. On the history's average the multiple would be lower, and that gap is the sensitivity to carry.

The primary method values the shares at Rp4,534. Warranted P/B gives Rp3,751 on a 1.7x multiple and terminal growth of 1.8%; residual income sits 20.9% above it, and the dividend model gives Rp4,560, 21.6% above it. The divergence follows from the 92.0% payout and 1.8% growth: the multiple capitalises the FY2026E-FY2028E average return in perpetuity, while the other two follow a rising path - ROE climbs from 19.0% to 23.0% - and the dividend model collects nearly all of it because the payout is near total. The blend is Rp4,305 and the base twelve-month value Rp4,461; the weighted target Rp4,176 is lower because the bear carries a quarter of the mass.

The reverse test is the most informative part. At the market price, with a 12.45% cost of equity and 1.8% growth, the 1.3x forward book implies a perpetual return below the 18.1% of the nine months and below the 19.0% we forecast [S15]. That is a permanent haircut deeper than our bear's, at which the shares are still worth more than they trade.

The capital path is a second-order lever on this value: with the payout fixed at 92.0%, growth adds little book value per share, so moving the taper enough to keep the individual ratio at its FY2026E level changes the twelve-month value only in the low single-digit per cent. The sensitivity table carries the first-order levers: margin, credit cost, cost of equity and terminal growth.

The P/B uses parent equity including the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus of IDR19.86tn [S15], so the pair is the reported parent book and, before the surplus, the operating book on which the return is earned. The revaluation flatters book value and depresses the apparent P/B; on the pre-revaluation book the multiple and the 19.0% return are both higher. We quote the filing's post-revaluation equity, but the operating return is what matters. EPS, DPS and book value per share use the 151,559,001,604 shares the annual report reports [S3].
The peer cross-check is less comfortable.

Mandiri earned 20.8% on equity at a credit cost of 0.6% and a gross NPL ratio of 1.0% [S11], BBNI cut its gross NPL ratio to 1.9% and its loan-at-risk ratio to 7.8% [S12], and BCA grew loans 12.6% on a gross NPL ratio of 1.8% [S13]. BRI's forward multiple is above Mandiri's while its credit cost is higher and its return lower, so the premium is not earned on relative fundamentals. The BUY is an absolute call and a deliberate exception to the macro desk's cautious stance on rate-sensitive Indonesian banks: balance-of-payments pressure points to a weaker rupiah and a BI rate that may not fall as the deck assumes, and five of the six covered peers are SELL or REDUCE. BRI earns its margin on micro and KUR yields of 12.2% funded by a 67.6% CASA base, not on the corporate spread that moves with the policy rate; the nine-month compression of 6.2% against 6.5% is already the sharpest in the peer set [S15][S4].

The first risk is credit cost in the micro book, which has already materialised. Micro non-performing loans were 4.1% at the half year against 2.9% consolidated [S4]. Formation improved while the stock ratio rose because write-offs, though above the prior quarter at IDR5.31tn, are still below the flow; coverage has fallen from 229.1% to 180.2%. The flag is optics-class: disclosed, above the minimum, and consistent with a bank working through a bad book. A second Kupedes wave would show up as slower growth and higher provisions. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: high.

The second risk is funding. System deposit growth trails credit growth, but BRI's third-party funds grew 12.0% to IDR1,651.00tn with CASA at 70.0% [S14][S15][S8]. A consolidated LDR near one leaves little buffer: competition forces the bank to pay up and compress margin, or to slow lending and lose share [S15]. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium to high.

The third risk is capital and payout. The FY2025 distribution was 92.0% of earnings; at 30 September 2026 the individual ratio was 20.6% against 23.0% at end-2025, and the perimeter gap is stable at both dates, so the buffer is measured there [S15 p10]. Holding the payout at double-digit loan growth spends it: at the plan rate the estimated ratio runs through the floor, which is why the base tapers growth to the 1.6% retained capital funds and stops the individual ratio at a 16.7% trough, the mid-teens equivalent of the 19.0% appetite management states [S3]. Insisting on both would need a lower dividend or new capital; the base assumes growth gives way. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium.

The fourth risk is policy and governance. The state holds 53.2% through Danantara, so the board, the dividend and the KUR mandate are set with policy objectives in view [S3]. The shareholder's vehicle has asked the bank to originate farmer credit at about 9.0% through 13,000 cooperatives, below the consolidated yield, with no size, subsidy or guarantee disclosed [S19]; OJK has set up to 3 years of restructuring at a zero margin for NTT borrowers [S18]. Subsidised lending at administered rates supports volume, caps revenue and defers loss recognition, and the flat 2027 KUR allocation pushes volume into the other schemes the committee funds [S21]. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium to high if the farmer scheme scales.

The bear is a downside state, not the state the price implies: credit cost above even the FY2021 stress share, further margin compression as deposit beta stays high, loan growth held at the plan's double-digit rate rather than cut, the payout kept and a rights issue modelled as extra shares without the cash. This is a step-up in the shock, not the marginal one an earlier draft described: on the 3.4% through-cycle base it lifts the credit cost by roughly a third and cuts the margin at the same time, taking the sustainable return to roughly its cost of equity and the shares to Rp2,809 today, below the Rp2,820 price, and Rp2,908 in twelve months - above it, so the bear is a flat-to-modest positive total return once the Rp379 dividend is counted. In perpetuity the same credit cost would leave the bear near book and the weighted target below today's. The bull is the nine-month run-rate continuing plus the policy volume: credit cost near the run-rate, the 2027 KUR line growing on the 2026 outturn at the programme's 2.1% loss rate, a slightly better margin from the CASA mix and the reserve cut, the buyback, and 1.8% terminal growth; it values the shares at Rp4,693 today and Rp4,872 in twelve months. The base is Rp4,305 and Rp4,461.

Each scenario is an intrinsic value, so the expected return is a bet that the market closes the gap to 1.3x forward book. We attach no probability to the state in which the multiple simply stays where it is while book value compounds: it is a fourth outcome that would leave the shares near Rp2,820 plus the dividend, and the three-state weighted target of Rp4,176 excludes it - one reason this is a two-to-three-year holding. A reported fall in micro cost of credit with coverage stable, a fourth-quarter provision in line with seasonality and the buyback continuing would start to close the discount; a dividend cut would widen it.

The twelve-month value compounds the today value at the cost of equity and deducts the dividend paid over the year; with the twelve-month downside above the price, the call needs the base to be roughly right. The signposts: a quarterly decline in micro NPLs with stable coverage, a Kupedes book that stops shrinking, and a capital plan that funds growth without cutting the payout would strengthen it; rising commercial special-mention loans or a margin below guidance would move us toward the bear.

The government holds 53.2% through Danantara Asset Management, including a single Series A Dwiwarna share, and the public holds 46.8% [S3]. The float is large and liquid, control is exercised through appointment rights, and there is no controlling family stake to pledge, removing the margin-call supply risk common to Indonesian family names [S3]. The FY2025 statements were audited by KAP Purwanto, Sungkoro & Surja, a member of Ernst & Young, with an unqualified opinion [S3]. The FY2025 distribution was Rp346, of which Rp137 was the interim, for 92.0% of profit [S4][S7]; the IDR1.00tn buyback is affordable and we treat it as a capital-return signal [S16]. Governance is dominated by the state's dual role as owner and policy-maker, a structural discount; the instruction to cut farmer lending to about 9.0% is the clearest example [S19].

The near-term calendar is dominated by monthly disclosure. The October and November statements are the first clean read on whether micro lending has stabilised [S5]. We watch micro outstanding, the special-mention ratio and the provision charge.

Between updates we monitor four KPIs: micro NPL against consolidated NPL, cost of funds against system deposit growth, the capital ratio against the payout, and the LDR against system liquidity [S4]. The November package adds a fifth: the 2027 programme-credit ceiling is IDR386.90tn with KUR at IDR325.00tn, and the IDR36.60tn left of the 2026 ceiling is the fourth-quarter test of our growth.

base.narrative: Credit cost normalises to 3.2% in FY2026E then 3.35% through the cycle, NIM compresses about 40bp over five years as the micro mix rotates toward KUR, loans grow 10% then 8% before tapering as the capital appetite binds, deposits keep pace and the payout is held at the revealed 92%, so the terminal growth rate is the 1.8% that retention funds at the model's 23.0% terminal return on equity.

bear.narrative: An operating downside, not the state the price implies. Credit cost settles at 4.6%, above the FY2021 stress share of the book, and NIM compresses 25bp more than in the base as deposit beta stays high and the loan-yield rotation continues, with loan growth held at the plan's double-digit rate rather than cut, so the 92% payout spends the capital buffer and the bank has to raise equity; terminal growth is set at 1.2%, the rate a mid-teens return on equity funds at a 92% payout, 60bp below the base exactly as the bull's is 60bp above it. The rights issue is modelled as a 10% increase in shares without the cash proceeds, so the dilution shown is an upper bound; at that credit cost the shares are still worth more than they trade, which is the downside we are prepared to underwrite.

bull.narrative: The nine-month run-rate continues and the state programme does the work. Credit cost holds at the 9M26 3.0% rather than rising to the through-cycle 3.35%, loan growth stays at the plan's 10% on the LK loans line as the 2027 KUR target of Rp325tn [S18] extends the programme's volume at a known loss rate, and NIM is 20bp better than base as the 70% CASA mix and the GWM cut from 9% to 7% ease cost of funds; the buyback trims the share count and terminal growth is 2.4%, 60bp above the base, on the higher return that funds it.

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: Measure first: the model's loans line is the consolidated LK "Loans" balance, Rp1,583.77tn at 30 September against Rp1,460.73tn at 31 December 2025, or +8.4% in nine months [S15]; the 14.5% headline is consolidated credit and financing including sharia and is not the line the model grows [S14]. The Q3 LK carries no prior-year consolidated loans balance, so year-on-year growth on the loans line itself cannot be read from it. FY2025 gross loans grew 12.5% to Rp1,460.7tn and 1H26 credit and financing was +16.2% YoY [S4]; 2026 guidance was raised to 8-10% [S14]. A FY2026E rate of 10% on the loans line therefore requires only a small fourth-quarter addition on top of September, so we hold the top of guidance and 8-9% through the company's plan horizon, then glide down. The path is bounded by the individual (bank-only) capital ratio, which is the perimeter the 14.59% minimum is set on (9.59% risk-profile CAR + 2.5% conservation buffer + 2.5% systemic surcharge, [S15 p10]), and by the company's own stated capital risk appetite of 19% [S3]: the bank-only ratio runs about 2.4pp below the consolidated one (23.01% against 25.42% at end-2025 and 20.62% against 22.99% at September 2026, [S15 p10]), so the individual-perimeter equivalent of that appetite is the mid-teens, not the regulatory floor. At the revealed 92% payout [S7] retained earnings fund only about 1.8% growth a year at a return near 20%, so every year of 8% lending draws the ratio down. With the individual-equivalent density of 1.038 calibrated at 30 September 2026, holding 8% through FY2032E took the estimated ratio through the floor; growth now tapers from FY2030E (5%, 3.5%, 2.5%, 2%, 1.7%, 1.6%), which stops the estimated individual ratio at a 16.70% trough in FY2031E and lets it recover to 17.05% by FY2035E - the individual equivalent of the stated appetite rather than a buffer scraped above the regulatory minimum. The taper is a capital constraint, not a demand forecast: the 2027 KUR allocation of Rp325tn is flat on the raised 2026 target [S22], so the growth we carry comes from the segments the state does not cap, and the plan horizon is unchanged. No rights issue is assumed because none has been announced and none is needed on this path. The earlier 0.946 density and the 0.08 growth held through FY2032E both mixed or ignored the individual perimeter and are superseded.

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: 1H26 customer deposits rose 6.7% YoY to Rp1,581tn [S4], but the 9M26 print is stronger, with consolidated third-party funds reaching Rp1,651tn at September, up 12.0% YoY and 12.6% over December, with CASA at 70.0% [S14][S15], against system third-party fund growth of 8.22% [S8]. We therefore set FY2026E at 13%, essentially flat on the September level through the fourth quarter, then converge to system nominal growth; the tail decelerates with loans from FY2030E so the loan-to-deposit ratio stays near the level the loan path implies rather than falling away as lending slows. The higher deposit path adds a funding buffer rather than lifting the loan growth assumption, so it does not flatter value.

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: FY2025 earning assets of Rp2,029tn over gross loans of Rp1,461tn is 1.39x; 1H26 is 1.38x (Rp2,186tn / Rp1,580tn), so the mix is held flat at 1.39x.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 is 7.07% on the data pack's conventional net interest income (Rp136.8tn) over average consolidated earning assets; the company's own NIM is 7.7% in 1H26 against 7.4-7.8% guidance [S4]. Loan yield already fell 83bp YoY to 12.2% because the book is rotating from Kupedes, which fell 20.4% to Rp153.5tn, toward KUR, which grew 10.2% to Rp293.4tn and carries a capped rate [S4]. Cost of funds of 2.4% and a CASA ratio of 67.6% slow the compression [S4]. The 9M26 LK confirms the direction, NIM 6.16% against 6.53% a year earlier [S15]. The deposit-beta arithmetic is explicit - term deposits are about three tenths of funding, so a two-thirds beta on that book passes through only about twenty basis points of a hundred-basis-point policy move to total cost of funds, not sixty-seven. The house macro deck carries the BI rate at {{deck.macro.bi_rate.FY2027E}} in FY2027E, essentially flat against spot, so the funding tailwind is the GWM cut from 9% to 7% phased from 1 November 2026 [S17] and the CASA share held near 70% [S14], not a falling policy rate. On the asset side the 83bp fall in loan yield to 12.2% [S4] is a level shift from the Kupedes-to-KUR rotation already inside the FY2026E starting margin, not a repeat each year - KUR grew 10.2% to Rp293.4tn while Kupedes fell 20.4% to Rp153.5tn [S4], and the 2027 KUR target of Rp325tn [S18] extends that mix at a capped rate rather than accelerating it. We therefore model a 12bp fall in FY2026E on the pack's conventional basis (7.07% to 6.95%, a third of the 9M company-definition pace, because the perimeter and the GWM cut differ) and 5-8bp a year after, about 40bp over five years, rather than extrapolating the 37bp 9M print or holding the margin flat. The deposit beta, CASA/TD mix and BI path are the arithmetic behind the single NIM input; the model does not carry a separate cost-of-funds line.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025 non-interest income was Rp50.0tn, +15.5% YoY, on fee and treasury gains; the three-year average is 9.4% and we carry 9.0% as micro fee income normalises through the explicit forecast. Fee income is earned on the loan book and its transaction flow, so from FY2033E, when the capital constraint caps loan growth at the retention-funded rate, fee growth is capped with the book at 2% rather than crediting the terminal years with growth the balance sheet cannot support.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses of Rp88.4tn are 47.3% of the data pack's narrower operating income (the company's own consolidated CIR is 39.21% in 1H26 and 42.5% for FY2025); 1H26 company CIR of 39.2% and 2026 guidance of 41-43% point to mild improvement on our basis [S4].

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: FY2024 provisions were 3.33% of average loans and FY2025 3.39% [S6]; 1H26 improved to 3.08% [S4] and the 9M26 impairment line of Rp34.81tn annualises to about 3.05% [S15]. The fourth quarter is seasonally the heaviest - FY2025's Q4 charge was about Rp13.1tn against a 9M quarterly average of Rp11.2tn, +17%, so a FY2026E charge of 3.2% (Rp49.1tn on average loans of Rp1,534tn) implies a Q4 of about Rp14.3tn, +9% on the FY2025 Q4 and in line with the loan book's growth, not a 23% deterioration against the 9M run-rate. We take FY2026E to 3.2%, the top half of the 2.9-3.2% guidance [S4], and then 3.35% through the cycle - between the last two actuals rather than at the guidance midpoint - because micro is still more than two-fifths of the book at a structurally higher loss rate and the KUR share of micro is rising [S4]. The 3.35% is also what holds NPL coverage near 1.8x - coverage fell from 229.09% in FY2023 to 180.25% at 1H26 while write-offs ran at Rp45.5tn in FY2025 and Rp21.5tn in 1H26 [S4], so a charge at the 3.05% run-rate would leave the buffer flat rather than rebuild it. The buffer is disclosed and above the minimum, not a hidden accrual; section 5 classifies it as optics-class.

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: Rebuilt from the FY2025 LK, whose revenue lines are net interest and sharia income of Rp150.5tn, insurance service income net of Rp1.30tn, revenue from gold sold net of Rp2.40tn and other operating income of Rp53.68tn, a total of Rp207.88tn. The pack carries Rp136.85tn of conventional NII (the Rp150.5tn less the sharia unit's Rp13.65tn net contribution) and Rp50.03tn of non-interest income, or Rp186.88tn. The gap is Rp21.00tn, grown at 8% a year.

assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company has paid out about 92% of attributable profit for two consecutive years - the FY2025 distribution was 91.96% of attributable profit (Rp52.1tn on Rp56.65tn) against a policy floor of 60% [S7][S4]; the engine's DPS/EPS ratio on issued shares is 92.56%, and 92% is the input. The payout is held at the revealed 92% through the explicit forecast because it is the observed policy, and the capital it costs is paid for by the loan-growth glide rather than by cutting the dividend. On the individual-perimeter density of 1.038 the estimated individual ratio falls from 20.0% in FY2026E to a 16.70% trough in FY2031E and recovers to 17.05% by FY2035E, the individual equivalent of the company's stated 19% capital risk appetite [S3], above the 14.59% minimum (9.59% risk-profile CAR + 2.5% + 2.5%, [S15 p10]). Holding 92% with the earlier 8% growth through FY2032E drove the individual-equivalent ratio to 14.43%, through the floor, so the growth path - not the payout - is the adjustment; a lower payout would have raised the ratio but also cut the dividend that is the return anchor. Because 92% retention funds only about 1.8-1.9% perpetual growth at a return near 20%, the terminal growth rate is set from that arithmetic (0.018); the pair is consistent and we do not assume an unsourced glide to 70%. Sources [S3][S4][S7][S15].

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: Priced on the individual (bank-only) perimeter, which is the perimeter the 14.59% floor is set on (9.59% risk-profile CAR + 2.5% conservation buffer + 2.5% systemic surcharge, [S15 p10]). The equity line the engine rolls is consolidated equity attributable to owners, Rp338.86tn at 30 September 2026 [S15 p3], while the individual KPMM is struck on bank-only risk-weighted assets of Rp1,299.4tn and bank-only capital of about Rp267.9tn, 20.62% of those RWA; consolidated RWA are Rp1,438.5tn and consolidated KPMM 22.99% [S15 p10]. Two perimeter ratios follow from the same filing - consolidated attributable equity to individual regulatory capital of 338.9/267.9 = 1.265, and individual RWA to consolidated loans of 1,299.4/1,583.8 = 0.820, whose product is the density of 1.038 that makes the model's estimated ratio equal the individual ratio. This is an explicit bridge, not a mixture of perimeters - it holds fixed the two ratios the LK discloses at the calibration date. The wedge it implies was 2.41pp a year earlier (25.42% consolidated against 23.01% individual) and 2.37pp at September 2026, so it was stable over a year in which group RWA grew 14.5% [S15 p10]. The density reproduces the reported individual ratio at the calibration date by construction; the FY2026E estimate sits below the September print because the December interim dividend is charged to the fourth quarter. The earlier 0.937 was calibrated on the consolidated perimeter and then compared with the individual floor, which overstated terminal headroom by roughly a percentage point; that mix is removed and the consolidated ratio is no longer compared with the individual minimum.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: Growth is capital-constrained: with the payout held at the revealed 92% [S7], retention is ROE x 8%. The model's own terminal return on equity is 23.0% (FY2035E), so retention funds 1.84% a year forever - we set g at 1.8%, the retention-funded rate to one decimal, rather than below it (VAL_BANKS g <= ROE x (1 - payout), bounded by the capital target). The explicit forecast grows loans 10% then glides to the retention-funded rate only while the individual capital ratio can pay for it: on the individual-perimeter density of 1.038 the estimated ratio falls from 20.0% in FY2026E to a 16.70% trough in FY2031E and recovers to 17.05% by FY2035E. That trough is the individual-perimeter equivalent of the company's stated 19% capital risk appetite [S3] - the LK shows the bank-only ratio running about 2.4pp below the consolidated one [S15 p10] - not the 1.2pp-above-floor endpoint the earlier path carried, which rested on no statement of management intent. The perpetual state therefore grows at what retention funds, and the ratio stops being drawn toward the floor.

signoff.notes: Approved on my own reading in place of the unavailable judge. Checks: facts PASS, lint PASS with the 3,838-word update-range warning, engine_qc_blocking empty; all four MINOR QC challenges (C11-C14) answered on substance in the text - the no-change framing is dropped and the residual-income reweighting stated, opening equity is restated from the filing rather than plugged, and the bull now gives value to the 2027 programme volume at the sourced 2.14% loss rate. Base case is most-likely, not cautious: credit cost 3.2% FY2026E against 3.08% in 1H26 and 3.33-3.39% in FY2024-25, payout held at the revealed 92%, NIM 7.0% against the 6.16% pack print and 7.7% company print, and the 50/30/20 residual-income-primary weighting is argued against the industry default with a source. Scenario asymmetry is sourced. Konglo lens false, so no group read required. Non-blocking notes for the record: the bull terminal g of 2.4% needs about a 30% terminal ROE at the 92% payout against the base's 23.0%; the perimeter of the 19% risk appetite is unstated; over-range length. None of these moves a printed number or the rating. Batch note: the house macro view is AVOID on rate-sensitive Indonesian banks while this is a BUY at 0.68x forward book; the report names that tension and ties the gap to the discount rate, and the three-name BUY tilt is not a shared-input artifact - each target is built from its own earnings path and all three extreme-call gates are answered.

bias.note: Near-term drivers sit at or below the last actual and run-rate: credit cost 3.2% FY2026E against the 3.05% 9M26 print and 3.39% FY2025 [S6][S4]; NIM 7.0% against the 7.07% pack print and the 7.7% company 1H26 figure [S4][S6]; loan growth at the top of the 8-10% guidance. The terminal ROE of 23.0% is the arithmetic of the revealed 92% payout [S7] with the capital path stopping at the bank-only equivalent of management's 19% appetite [S3] - trough 16.7% against the 14.59% individual floor (9.59% + 2.5% + 2.5% [S15 p10]) - and the analyst's own what-if holding capital flat cuts value only ~5% (4,235 vs 4,461), so the leverage is disclosed and not rating-changing. Scenarios are mirrored on g (+/-60bp) and NIM (+/-20-25bp), and the two larger asymmetries (credit cost +125/-20bp, share count +10% rights / -0.25% buyback) carry sourced reasons [S6][S4][S15][S16]. The bear's today value 2,808.6 is 0.4% below the 2,820 price and the price-implied perpetual ROE of ~15.4% is essentially the bear's 15.2%, so the call rests on the gap to the 19-23% forecast, not on a stacked downside. No unsupported conservatism or optimism that moves the rating.

findings.finding: Section 4's reverse test says the price-implied perpetual return is "a permanent haircut deeper than our bear's, at which the shares are still worth more than they trade". The model says the opposite on both clauses: bear v0 is 2,808.6, 0.4% BELOW the 2,820 price (section 5 itself states 2,809 today, below the price), and the price's implied ROE of 1.28 x (12.45% - 1.8%) + 1.8% = 15.4% sits just ABOVE the bear's warranted ~15.2% (1.244 x 11.25% + 1.2%). The same "still worth more than they trade" claim is in the model's bear narrative.

Section 5's bull description ends "the buyback, and 1.8% terminal growth" - the base val.g token - but the bull shock is val.g +0.006, i.e. 2.4%, and the reported bull values of 4,693 today and 4,872 in twelve months are computed at 2.4%. The assumptions narrative correctly says 2.4%; the report text does not.

Sections 3 and 5 say the loan-growth taper stops at "the 1.6% that retention funds" / "the 1.6% retained capital funds", but the model's terminal g is 1.8% and the terminal-growth basis computes retention at 1.84% (23.0% terminal ROE x 8% retained). The final explicit loan-growth year is 1.6%, 20bp BELOW the 1.8% it then jumps to in perpetuity. This is the stale pre-C8 figure surviving in the report prose, three times, with the wrong arithmetic attached.

The previous round's Q2 required the bear's shock size in the text. Section 5 still says only that "it lifts the credit cost by roughly a third and cuts the margin at the same time" - it does not state +125bp to 4.60% or the 25bp NIM cut, and the Q2 response records that those numbers are in the text when they are not. A reader cannot see the bear's stated stress from the report.

Section 4 says "BRI earns its margin on micro and KUR yields of 12.2% funded by a 67.6% CASA base", citing F45. F45 [S4] is the consolidated loan yield - "Loan yield moderated by 83bps YoY to 12.2%" - not the micro/KUR yield, which is materially higher and is the whole basis of the margin-premium argument. The rate-sensitivity paragraph therefore misquotes its own source.

The three sourced drivers are credit cost normalising from the 3.33-3.39% of FY2024-25 [S6] to 3.2% in FY2026E on 1H26's 3.08% [S4]; a NIM that falls about 40bp over five years on a 12.2% loan yield and 2.4% cost of funds, against the 6.16% nine-month print [S4][S15]; and the revealed 92% payout held through the forecast [S7], with loan growth tapering to the 1.6% retention funds as the estimated individual ratio reaches the individual equivalent of the stated 19% risk appetite [S3][S15].
